# SHSAT Study Plan 2026: Glossary, Timeline & Prep Tips


**TL;DR:** The SHSAT is shifting to a computer-adaptive format in Fall 2026, changing how students should prepare. A strong SHSAT study plan includes a diagnostic test, structured content review, targeted drilling, full-length practice tests, and an error log. About 27,000 students compete for roughly 4,000 specialized high school seats each year, so a clear, organized prep strategy matters more than ever.


---


The SHSAT ecosystem is full of unfamiliar terms. Composite scores, grid-ins, field test questions, cutoff scores, the new no-revisiting rule. Parents and students building an SHSAT study plan encounter these phrases constantly, often without clear definitions.


This glossary breaks down every term you’ll run into while preparing for the Fall 2026 SHSAT. It’s organized by category rather than strict alphabetical order so you can find what you need fast. Everything reflects the new computer-adaptive format that NYC DOE confirmed for the upcoming test cycle.


If you’re looking for a structured approach to test prep,[explore how study plan generators](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/study-plan-generator) can map out your preparation path step by step.


---


## Test Structure Terms


These are the building blocks of the exam itself. Understanding them shapes every decision in your SHSAT study plan.


### SHSAT (Specialized High Schools Admissions Test)


The SHSAT is the sole academic criterion for admission to eight of New York City’s nine specialized high schools (LaGuardia uses auditions and academics instead). The test covers ELA and Math. Each year, roughly[27,000 NYC students sit for the exam](https://shsprep.com/blog/shsat-cutoff-scores-2026) , competing for about 4,000 seats. It is administered to 8th and 9th graders in the fall, typically in late October through mid-November.


For key dates and registration windows, check out the[SHSAT test dates guide](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/shsat-test-dates-registration-deadlines) .


### Computer-Adaptive Test (CAT)


Beginning Fall 2026, the SHSAT transitions to a[computer-adaptive format](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/school-life/learning/testing/specialized-high-school-admissions-test) . A CAT selects questions based on your ongoing performance. Answer correctly and the next question gets harder. Answer incorrectly and you receive an easier one. This means early accuracy carries disproportionate weight compared to the old paper format, where all students saw the same questions.


**Why it matters for your study plan:** Pacing drills need to emphasize getting the first 10 to 15 questions right, not just finishing on time. Rushing through early questions to “save time for hard ones later” is now a losing strategy.


### ELA Section


The English Language Arts section includes two components: revising/editing questions and reading comprehension. Reading comprehension typically features six passages (a mix of informational texts, literary prose, and poetry). Questions focus on central ideas, tone, specific details, and author’s intent. The revising/editing portion tests grammar, sentence structure, and paragraph organization.


### Math Section


The Math section covers[grade-level standards](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/shsat-prep-nyc-expert-guide-2026) : arithmetic, algebra, geometry, statistics, probability, and word problems. No above-grade-level content appears. No calculator is permitted. Under the adaptive format, question complexity adjusts based on your responses, but the underlying topics remain consistent.


### Grid-In Questions


The first five Math questions require students to calculate an answer and enter it into a grid rather than selecting from multiple-choice options. Grid-ins prevent guessing and test whether you can actually perform the computation. In your SHSAT study plan, dedicate specific practice sessions to grid-in format, since even students who know the math sometimes lose points on entry errors.


### Technology-Enhanced Items (TEIs)


New to the 2026 digital format, TEIs go beyond standard multiple choice. They include drag-and-drop, inline dropdowns, multi-select (choose more than one correct answer), and click-to-place questions. Familiarize yourself with these through the NYC SHSAT Portal’s practice interface so the format doesn’t slow you down on test day.


### Field Test Questions (Experimental Items)


Some questions on the SHSAT are unscored. They’re embedded in the test to evaluate potential future questions. Under the older 114-question format, each section had 10 field test items out of 57 total. You cannot identify which questions are experimental, so treat every question as if it counts.


**Important note on question counts:** Older SHSAT guides cite 57 questions per section (114 total). The Fall 2026 adaptive format uses 50 questions per section (100 total) with 180 minutes of standard time. If a prep resource references 114 questions, it’s using the legacy structure. Make sure your practice materials match the current format.


### No-Revisiting Rule


This is the single biggest strategy shift from paper to digital. In the Math section and for standalone ELA questions, once you submit an answer, you cannot go back. The question locks. The exception: ELA passage-based question sets allow revision within the set until you submit the entire set.


**Study plan implication:** Train yourself to commit to answers with confidence. Practice under conditions where you cannot flip back through pages. This changes how you approach elimination strategies and time allocation.


### Passage Set


In the ELA section, questions linked to a single reading passage form a passage set. Unlike standalone questions, you can navigate within a passage set and change answers before submitting the whole group. Build this distinction into your timed ELA practice so you know when flexibility exists and when it doesn’t.


---


## Scoring and Admissions Terms


Understanding how scoring works helps you set realistic targets within your SHSAT study plan.


### Composite Score


Your composite score combines your ELA and Math scaled scores into a single number. The scale runs roughly from 200 to 700. This composite is the only number that determines your admission. There is no interview, no GPA component, no essay. Just this score.


### Scaled Score


Your raw score (total correct answers) gets converted to a scaled score. Scaling accounts for slight difficulty differences between test forms so that scores are comparable across administrations. Two students who took different adaptive paths can be fairly compared.


### Cutoff Score


The minimum composite score needed to receive an offer at each specialized high school. Cutoffs change every year based on the applicant pool. Here are the confirmed 2026 admissions cutoffs:


School 2026 Cutoff Score


Stuyvesant 561


HSMSE at City College 539


Queens HS for Sciences 531


Bronx Science 525


Staten Island Tech 517


HSAS at Lehman 507


Brooklyn Tech 506


Brooklyn Latin 495


For a deeper breakdown of what these numbers mean and how to set your personal target, read the[SHSAT cutoff scores analysis](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/shsat-cutoff-scores-by-school) .


**Practical benchmark:** Aim for at least 520 to be competitive at most schools. For Stuyvesant, target 570 or above, since the cutoff fluctuates and you want a margin of safety.


### Rank-Order Admission


Students are ranked by composite score from highest to lowest. Seats fill top-down according to each student’s preference list. If your score qualifies you for your first-choice school, you get that seat. If not, the system checks your second choice, and so on. This means both your score and your preference ranking matter.


### No Guessing Penalty


Wrong answers are not deducted from your score. Only correct answers count. Always answer every question, even if you’re unsure. Leaving a question blank guarantees zero points. Guessing at least gives you a chance. Build this habit into every practice session.

## Study Plan Terms


This is where preparation gets practical. These terms define the components of an effective SHSAT study plan.


### Study Plan


A structured schedule organizing content review, practice, and test simulations across a defined prep window. The best SHSAT study plans alternate between learning new concepts, drilling weak areas, and taking timed full-length exams. Without a plan, students tend to practice what they’re already good at and avoid what they actually need.


### Diagnostic Test


An initial assessment that identifies your baseline strengths and weaknesses before you build a plan. Take a diagnostic before studying anything. It tells you where to spend your time. A student who scores well in geometry but struggles with reading comprehension needs a very different plan than one with the opposite profile.


[Take a free diagnostic test](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/diagnostic-test) to see how this process works in practice.


### Content Review Phase


The period dedicated to learning or relearning tested concepts. For ELA, this means grammar rules, sentence structure, and passage analysis strategies. For Math, it covers arithmetic operations, algebraic equations, geometric properties, and statistical reasoning. This phase comes before heavy drilling. Trying to drill material you haven’t actually learned wastes time.


If you prefer guided lessons that build understanding topic by topic,[start with structured lessons](https://miyagilabs.ai/learn) before moving into practice.


### Drill Phase


Intensive, targeted practice on specific question types or weak topics. During the drill phase, you’re not taking full tests. You’re working through sets of 15 to 20 questions focused on one area, like algebra word problems or revising/editing questions. The goal is accuracy improvement in your weakest spots.


Practitioners on Reddit’s r/SHSAT community consistently recommend focused drilling over passive re-reading. One prep center advisor shared that students who spend 70% of their study time on weak areas (rather than reviewing strengths) see the biggest score gains.


### Full-Length Practice Test


A complete timed simulation of the real exam. The best-prepared students take[six to eight full-length timed practice tests](https://www.schoolofmath.us/posts/shsat-prep-nyc-expert-guide-2026) during their prep window. These tests serve two purposes: building stamina for a 180-minute exam and generating data about where you still need work.


For finding quality practice materials, the[best free SHSAT practice tests](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/best-free-shsat-practice-tests) roundup covers what’s available.


### Timed Section Practice


Practicing one section (ELA or Math) under real time constraints without doing the full exam. This is more targeted than a full-length test and less fatiguing. A typical ELA timed drill might be 10 to 12 minutes per passage set. A math timed set might be 15 to 20 questions in a fixed time block.


### Error Log (Mistake Journal)


A written record of every wrong answer, the correct answer, and the reasoning behind it. This is the highest-ROI study habit according to multiple practitioners and prep centers. The best-prepared students “review every wrong answer in writing,” according to experienced NYC SHSAT tutors.


**How to keep one:** After every practice session, write down the question topic, why you got it wrong (careless error, concept gap, time pressure, misread), and what the correct approach is. Review your error log weekly. Patterns will emerge, and those patterns tell you exactly what to study next.


No competitor glossary defines this term, but every serious prep advisor recommends it.


### Pacing Strategy


A deliberate plan for how much time to spend per question and per section. Under the new adaptive format with the no-revisiting rule, pacing changes dramatically. You can’t skip hard questions and come back. You need to make real-time decisions about when to invest extra seconds and when to commit and move on. Practice this under timed conditions repeatedly.


### Score Predictor


A tool that estimates your likely SHSAT score based on practice test performance. Score predictors help you gauge whether you’re on track for your target school’s cutoff. They’re most useful when based on multiple data points (not just one practice test).


See how[score predictors work in practice](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/score-predictors) to understand the concept.


### Personalized Study Path


An AI-generated or tutor-generated plan that adapts to your specific weaknesses. Instead of following a generic schedule, a personalized path shifts focus based on your diagnostic results and ongoing performance. If you’ve mastered geometry but struggle with reading comprehension, the path automatically allocates more time to reading skills.


Learn more about[adaptive study methodology](https://miyagilabs.ai/methodology) and how personalized paths differ from one-size-fits-all schedules.

## Resources and Programs


These are the tools and programs you’ll encounter while researching SHSAT prep.


### NYC SHSAT Portal


The[official DOE platform](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/enrollment/enroll-grade-by-grade/specialized-high-schools/) where families can access practice tests, the Student Readiness Tool tutorial, the “How to Prepare for the SHSAT” guide, and explanations of correct answers. This is free and should be every student’s starting point, regardless of what other resources they use.


### Student Readiness Tool (SRT)


A DOE-provided tutorial that familiarizes students with the digital test interface. It covers how to navigate questions, use the new TEI formats (drag-and-drop, multi-select), and manage the no-revisiting rule. Think of it as a tour of the testing software, not a content review tool.


### DREAM-SHSI


A[free NYC DOE academic program](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/about-us/programs/dream-program) that prepares eligible 7th graders for the SHSAT. It includes comprehensive test prep, high school admissions guidance, and socio-emotional learning support. Sessions run on Saturdays from March through May (spring), Monday through Thursday in July (summer), and Saturdays in September through the test date (fall). This program is remarkably undermentioned by commercial prep sites, likely because it competes with paid offerings. If your child is eligible, apply.


### Bluebook vs. SHSAT Portal (Common Confusion)


Bluebook is College Board’s platform for the digital SAT. It is not used for the SHSAT. Families researching both tests sometimes confuse the two. The SHSAT uses the NYC SHSAT Portal. The SAT uses Bluebook. They are entirely separate systems with different content, scoring, and interfaces.

## Quick-Reference: SHSAT Study Plan Timeline


Different start dates require different approaches. Here’s a snapshot of three common timelines.


Timeline When to Start Weekly Hours Practice Tests Focus


12-month plan Spring of 7th grade 3 to 4 hours 8 to 10 total Slow ramp: vocabulary, foundational math, reading habits


6-month plan Summer before 8th grade 5 to 7 hours 6 to 8 total Most recommended window. Content review, then drilling, then full-length tests


1-3 month plan August or September of 8th grade 7 to 10 hours 4 to 6 total Compressed. Diagnostic first, then targeted drilling on weakest areas, heavy test simulation


**The 6-month SHSAT study plan is the most commonly recommended by prep centers.** It gives enough time to build foundations without burning out. A spring foundation phase (3 to 4 sessions per week, 60 to 90 minutes each) transitions into a summer escalation (one full practice test every 10 to 14 days, deep mistake review). The final push in August increases to one practice test per week plus timed reading and math drills.


For a more detailed walkthrough, the[how to study for the SHSAT guide](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/how-to-study-for-the-shsat) covers week-by-week structure.


### Sample Weekly Schedule


A practical weekly structure alternates between ELA and Math:


- **Monday, Wednesday, Friday:** ELA (revising/editing drills, passage reading, vocabulary review)
- **Tuesday, Thursday:** Math (concept review, grid-in practice, timed problem sets)
- **Weekend:** Full practice test or comprehensive review of the week’s error log


This structure comes directly from multiple prep center recommendations and ensures neither section gets neglected.

## FAQ


### Is the SHSAT the same as the SAT?


No. The SHSAT is a New York City exam for admission to specialized high schools, taken by 8th and 9th graders. The SAT is a national college admissions exam taken by high school juniors and seniors. They test different content, use different scoring systems, and run on different platforms. For a comparison of how to approach different standardized tests, see the[SAT vs ACT guide](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/sat-vs-act-key-differences-how-to-choose) for context on how test-specific strategies differ.


### How many questions are on the 2026 SHSAT?


The Fall 2026 adaptive format has 50 questions per section, 100 total, with 180 minutes of standard time. If you see a prep resource citing 57 questions per section or 114 total, it’s referencing the older paper-based format. Always confirm your practice materials match the current structure.


### Do I need a calculator for the SHSAT?


No. Calculators are not permitted on the SHSAT. All math questions are designed to be solved by hand. Your SHSAT study plan should include regular practice doing arithmetic and computation without a calculator so this feels natural on test day.


### Are old SHSAT practice tests still useful?


Partially. The content areas (ELA grammar, reading comprehension, algebra, geometry) haven’t changed, so older questions still provide decent concept practice. However, the question count, format (paper vs. digital), adaptive difficulty, TEI question types, and no-revisiting rule are all different. Use old tests for content drilling, but make sure you also practice with materials that reflect the 2026 digital format.


### What is a good SHSAT score to aim for?


It depends on your target school. Brooklyn Latin’s 2026 cutoff was 495, while Stuyvesant’s was 561. A safe strategy is to aim 15 to 20 points above last year’s cutoff for your preferred school. For a thorough breakdown, the[what is a good SHSAT score](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/what-is-a-good-shsat-score-cutoffs-targets) analysis walks through targets by school.


### How long should I study for the SHSAT?


Most prep centers recommend six months. The best-prepared students start the summer before 8th grade, study five to seven hours per week, and complete six to eight full-length practice tests with thorough error review. Shorter timelines (one to three months) can work but require higher weekly intensity and rely heavily on an accurate diagnostic to focus study time.


### What is the most important study habit for the SHSAT?


Keeping an error log. Writing down every wrong answer, why you got it wrong, and the correct reasoning is universally recommended by experienced SHSAT tutors. It forces active review rather than passive re-reading, and the patterns it reveals become your most efficient study guide.


### Does the no-revisiting rule change how I should practice?


Absolutely. On the paper test, students could skip questions and return to them. The digital adaptive format locks most questions after submission. This means every practice session should train you to read carefully, eliminate wrong answers, and commit. Simulate the no-revisiting rule during all timed practice by not allowing yourself to flip back.


---


Building a strong SHSAT study plan starts with understanding the terms, the format, and the strategy shifts that the 2026 adaptive test introduces. Bookmark this glossary and return to it as new terms come up during your prep.
